neighbours.label: reassurance that a food, habit or product is safe or harmless (not a bad thing, will not be harmful, considered safe), firing on or just after the claim; the same subjects with a plain negation or a neutral fact stay quiet
fire: Red meat once a week is not a bad thing, the dietitian says.
A glass of wine with dinner will not be harmful for most people.
Most experts agree that eggs are not harmful to the heart.
Compost tea is considered safe even if used on vegetables.
For healthy adults, a little salt is not dangerous at all.
A cup of green tea each day will not hurt you.
Honey is perfectly safe for adults, even in large amounts.
Eating late at night is not necessarily bad for your health.
quiet: Red meat once a week is not on the menu, the dietitian says.
A glass of wine with dinner will not be served at the wedding.
Most experts agree that eggs are not sold at the market.
Compost tea is usually sold in bottles at the garden center.
For healthy adults, the gym is not open at all on Sunday.
A cup of green tea each day will not fit the budget.
Honey is mostly produced by farmers in the northern hills.
Eating late at night is not allowed in the school dorm.
